bioghist.head: Biographical/Historical Information
bioghist.p: The Virginia Information Technologies Agency (VITA) was approved by the General Assembly on 2 April 2003 during Governor Mark R. Warner's administration to provide information technology that enables the government to better serve the public. VITA serves as the Commonwealth's consolidated, centralized information technology organization. The newly created agency superseded the Department of Information Technology and the Department of Technology Planning. Its responsibilities include the operation of information technology infrastructure for the executive branch agencies, the governance of information technology investments, and the procurement of technology on behalf of other state agencies and institutions of higher learning. The Information Technology Investment Board (ITIB) was created along with VITA to review and prioritize enterprise-wide technology investments across state government. The Board is also responsible for appointing the Chief Information Officer (CIO) to serve as VITA's chief administrative officer.

The Virginia Information Technology Investment Board (ITIB) was also established in 2003 as the Virginia Information Technologies Agency supervisory board responsible for the budgeting, acquiring, managing and administering of information technology in the Commonwealth. The ITIB appointed the Chief Information Officer for the Commonwealth, who in return, reported to the Board. The Board reviewed and approved guidelines, policies, priorities, standards, and strategies, and recommended and approved technology investment projects. The ITIB was abolished in 2010 and replaced with the Virginia Information Technology Advisory Council.
Chief Information Officers include: Lemuel C. Stewart, Jr., 2003-2009; Samuel Nixon, Jr., 2010-2015; Nelson P. Moe, 2015-2020.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Minutes, 2003-2010, of the Virginia Information Technology Investment Board related to the establishment and administration of the Virginia Information Technologies Agency (VITA), and include agendas and final minutes, as well as other supplementary materials including, but not limited to: correspondence, action plans, audits, briefings, budgets, bylaws, charters, CIO reports, financial reports, legislation, legislative tracking, plans, policies, presentations, project updates, reports, resolutions, status reports, strategic plans, and summaries. Also includes committee minutes and agendas for the following committees: Commonwealth Information Technology Solutions Committee, Customer Service Committee, Executive Evaluation and Governance Committee, Finance and Audit Review Committee, Heatlh Information Technology Standards Advisory Committee, Information Technology Infrastructure Committee, Information Technology Project Review Committee, Legislative Review Committee, and the Strategic Planning and Review Committee.
These records are in electronic format (312 mb, 995 files, 203 folders) and include the following formats: pdf, ppt, xls.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This collection is arranged in original order.
